title: The Signal Tower: Power the Valley
audienceRationale: The learner is nine, chose a competitive wrestling loss as a conversation topic (comfort with stakes, not proof of in-task resilience), explicitly requested harder riddles across sessions, noticed repeated riddles instantly, and challenged faulty riddle logic. This profile argues for: (1) a world with real internal logic that never cheats — every product must be visibly countable, because she audits logic; (2) fresh material with zero repeated situations, because she detects repetition and it costs trust; (3) escalation framed as invitation and curiosity ('there's a bigger circuit if you want it') rather than competition or ranking, because the wrestling-loss evidence does not establish that failure-framing motivates her in math and the charter explicitly flags this risk; (4) hints that are dignified and stepwise on request, matching her demonstrated pattern of asking for scaffolding and then continuing — hints are a tool she reaches for, never a rescue pushed at her. The theme (restoring power to a valley by wiring equal-group energy circuits) is deliberately non-babyish: it treats her as a competent engineer, consistent with a child who asks for harder problems.
openingPromise: A dark valley scene: a signal tower stands unlit at the center of a dim landscape with seven darkened districts (lunch hall, greenhouse, sticker workshop, carrot farm, library, stadium, and the tower itself). A single line of text: 'The valley's power runs on equal groups. Wire the circuits. Light the valley.' The promise is explicit and structural: every correct multiplication visibly restores power to one district, and the learner can see all seven dark districts from second one — the whole scope of the experience is legible at a glance, and the payoff (a fully lit valley) is previewed as silhouette.
firstThreeSeconds: Second 0–1: the valley fades in from black, districts as dark silhouettes with faint outlines, the tower pulsing one weak amber light. Second 1–2: the promise line types on ('Wire the circuits. Light the valley.') while the first district — the lunch hall — glows faintly and slides its scene forward: four lunch trays materialize one at a time with a soft placement sound, each visibly holding 3 apple slices. Second 2–3: two large glowing question panels rise beneath the trays — 'How many equal groups?' and 'How many in each group?' — with tappable number choices already lit and inviting. No menu, no tutorial screen, no name entry: the child is looking at a real countable situation and live buttons within three seconds.
firstAction: One tap. The learner taps a number choice under 'How many equal groups?' (choices 2, 3, 4, 5). The tap target is at least 88px, works identically for touch and mouse, and the moment it is touched the corresponding count animates in the scene: tapping '4' pulses each of the four trays in sequence with a counting tick, so even the very first action shows the mathematics gripping the world before anything is committed. Both questions (groups, amount per group) are visible simultaneously; nothing is committed until both are answered and the single 'Connect the wire' button is tapped, exactly per the item-01 response contract.
interactionDemonstration: The demonstration is diegetic, not a tutorial overlay. When item-01's trays appear, the tower sends a thin animated pulse of light down a wire toward the lunch hall that stops at an open switch — showing wordlessly that answering connects the circuit. As the learner hovers or rests a finger on any number choice, the scene previews that count non-committally (pulsing that many trays or that many slices on one tray), teaching the tap→world mapping through the world itself. The 'Connect the wire' commit button visibly closes the switch when both parts are chosen. By the end of item-01 the learner has experienced the full loop — choose, preview in the world, commit, world responds — with zero instructional text beyond the item's own prompt.
coreInteraction: Tap-to-choose and tap-to-place, never drag-precision, per the packet's input contracts. Each item is one district's circuit panel: the countable representation (trays, pots, sticker array, build grid, shelves, stadium) occupies the left ~60% of the 1365×768 frame; the response panel (choices, factor tiles, equation slots, or the multi-select toggles) occupies the right ~40%, all reachable without scrolling. Item-04's construction uses a tap-to-place grid: tap a row-start cell to open a row, tap to set how many carrots fill it; the system enforces uniform rows (structural integrity guard) but never auto-arranges or auto-fills. Committing any answer routes power: correct commits close the switch and send visible current through the wire into the district; the district's lights come on room by room in exactly the product's count (e.g., 20 tulip-lamps flare in the greenhouse for item-02), so the product is re-verified by the world's own reaction. Incorrect commits never punish — the current travels the wire, reaches the district, flickers, and returns, and the scene enters the packet-specified reasoning retry (re-count a highlighted row, re-check one equation) with all progress preserved.
mathAsPower: The mathematics is literally the power source. Groups × amount-per-group is framed as the valley's electrical law: a circuit only carries current when the number of equal groups and the amount in each group are both named truly. Wrong factors produce a mismatched circuit the world visibly rejects (flicker-and-return), correct factors produce current, and the product is the wattage — the district lights exactly that many lamps, countably. In item-04 the learner's own built array IS the circuit board: her construction physically becomes the wiring diagram that powers the carrot farm. In item-05, judging which equations match is framed as inspecting which of four fuse-cards fit the library's circuit — both valid orderings fit, and the world demonstrates the referent swap by re-tracing the same 30 book-lights first shelf-by-shelf (3 groups of 10) then in the other reading order, total unchanged. The child never does math to earn an unrelated reward; the math IS the mechanism, visibly and causally.
stakes: Diegetic and warm, never punitive: the valley is dark and its districts wait. Each district has a small silhouetted detail that lights only on completion (the greenhouse's tulips bloom in light, the stadium's pennants ripple). The stake is restoration — the learner can always see how much of the valley remains dark and that only she can light it. There is no timer, no lives, no score, no leaderboard, and no comparative framing anywhere, honoring the charter's warning that in mathematics difficulty must read as invitation rather than judgment. The optional item-06 stadium is the valley's biggest, brightest district — the stake of skipping it is only that its lights stay off unless she chooses it, and the valley still counts as fully restored on the standard path (the stadium shows a 'reserve circuit' glow rather than darkness if declined).
consequences: Correct: current flows, the district illuminates lamp-by-lamp in the product's exact count, the tower gains one steady beacon ring, and the valley map's silhouette brightens — cumulative, visible, and permanent within the session. Incorrect: the current flickers at the switch and returns without any breakage sound, alarm, red flash, or lost progress; the world responds as a patient circuit tester, not a judge. Each incorrect commit triggers exactly the packet's incorrectPath for that item: the representation stays (or, in item-04, the learner's build is preserved untouched), one relevant element is highlighted for re-counting or re-checking, and the learner re-decides. Feedback language names referents ('4 trays, 3 slices on each tray'), never states withheld products, never affirms a wrong answer, never rejects a right one, and never introduces shame vocabulary — the circuit 'isn't carrying yet,' it is never 'wrong, try again.'
recovery: Recovery is designed as re-engagement, not penalty, per the packet's universal reasoning-retry rule. On any miss: (1) the countable representation is re-exposed with one diagnostic element highlighted (one pot's tulips, one array row, one equation card); (2) the learner is asked to re-count or re-decide that one thing — the system never supplies the decision; (3) all committed correct work is preserved, including item-06's stage-one commit if stage two is missed, and item-04's built rows are never erased. Stepwise hints exist behind a small, dignified 'circuit notes' toggle — visually a tool, not a lifeline — surfaced as an available offer in items 02–07 and strictly on-request-only in item-06, matching each item's hintPolicy; no hint tier ever states a withheld product. Because the wrestling-loss evidence establishes only comfort discussing loss (asm-06 at 0.5 confidence), retry tone is deliberately neutral-curious rather than consoling: no 'don't worry!' language, just the circuit tester's calm re-highlight. Item-07 has no failure exit at all: unlimited re-answers, and the valley finale always plays.
progression: District 1 — Lunch Hall (item-01, opening orientation): name the two governing quantities for 4 trays of 3 slices; maximum support, both quantities as bounded choices, no product demanded, no failure state; establishes the tap→preview→commit loop diegetically.

District 2 — Greenhouse (item-02, Segment 1): representation and equation 5 × 4 = ? both given; learner supplies only the product 20 by counting or skip counting the tulips; stepwise hints become available as an offer.

District 3 — Sticker Workshop (item-03, Segment 2): first array, 6 rows of 7 stickers, no equation shown; learner names both factors with referents before the equation reveals, then supplies 42; exactly one new demand added (array language) while the representation stays given.

District 4 — Carrot Farm (item-04, Segment 3, responsibility-transfer point): words only, no picture; learner builds 8 rows of 6 on the tap-to-place grid, assembles 8 × 6 from factor tiles, supplies 48; system guards structural integrity but never auto-arranges; array or equal-groups builds both accepted.

District 5 — Library (item-05, Segment 4): 3 shelves of 10 books shown; learner judges four fuse-card equations, accepting both 3 × 10 = 30 and 10 × 3 = 30 and rejecting 3 + 10 = 13 and 10 × 10 = 100; the world traces the same 30 lights in both reading orders to show the referent swap without formal property names.

District 6 — Stadium (item-06, Segment 5, strictly elective): offered as 'the valley's biggest circuit — yours if you want it,' curiosity-framed with no competitive language; two-stage 9 × 9 = 81 then 7 × 9 = 63 with a banner covering 2 rows; hints on request only, nothing pushed; exit back to the standard tier at any time with all progress preserved and the stadium showing a reserve-circuit glow rather than darkness.

District 7 — The Tower (item-07, payoff consolidation): the learner's own saved carrot-farm build and library judgment are re-shown unaltered inside the tower; she states what each factor counted in her own 8 × 6 = 48 and in 3 × 10 = 30; unlimited re-answers, no failure exit; correct meaning statements light the tower's beacon and trigger the full-valley finale.
interactionContinuity: One interaction grammar persists across all seven districts: representation on the left, response panel on the right, tap-to-choose with non-committal in-world preview, a single 'Connect the wire' commit, current-flow feedback. What changes is only which parts of the circuit the learner owns — mirroring the packet's monotonic scaffold withdrawal exactly. In items 01–03 the representation is pre-wired and she supplies increasingly many values; in item-04 the same tap gesture that previously selected numbers now places carrots (same input verb, new authority); in item-05 the same toggle gesture judges equations; item-06 chains two commits on one persistent array; item-07 replays her own saved surfaces. Because the grammar never changes, no re-tutorializing is ever needed, and rising difficulty is experienced purely as rising ownership, not new controls.
worldReaction: The world reacts causally and countably to every mathematical act. Choice previews pulse the exact count chosen (choosing '7' per row pulses seven stickers in one row). Correct commits: current animates from tower to district, and the district illuminates in exactly the product's count of lamps, verifiable by eye — 12 tray-lights, 20 tulip-lamps, 42 sticker-glints, 48 carrot-row lights in the learner's own layout, 30 book-spines, 81 then 63 pennant-flickers, so the world itself performs the verification each item's correctAnswer demands. Incorrect commits: flicker-and-return at the switch plus the item-specific diagnostic highlight. The valley map accumulates: each lit district stays lit, the tower gains a beacon ring per district, ambient sky lightens stepwise from night toward dawn across the session, so global progress is readable at every moment without any score number. In item-05 the world explicitly demonstrates the factor-order insight by re-tracing identical lights in two orders; in item-07 the tower projects the learner's own prior builds as living circuit blueprints.
payoff: The finale is consolidation made spectacular, per asm-08. When item-07's meaning statements are committed correctly, the tower's beacon ignites and the camera pulls back to the whole valley at dawn — every district lit, the learner's own 8×6 carrot grid and 3-shelf library visible in miniature glowing exactly as she built and judged them. The tower then replays the full chain as a light-trace across the map, with the learner's own numbers: situation → equal groups and amount in each group → representation → equation → verified product, narrated in one calm line per link ('You found the groups. You built them. You wrote them. You counted them true.'). Nothing generic: every element in the finale is her completed work, per the item-07 validation rule. A final still frame of the lit valley with her two equations (8 × 6 = 48, 3 × 10 = 30) inscribed on the tower serves as the closing image. If item-06 was completed, the stadium's 81 pennants ripple in the finale wind as a visible extra.
replayVariation: Question content, answers, scope, and difficulty are frozen and never change — replay variation lives entirely in the mutable layer. On replay: district visual skins rotate (night-rain, snow-dusk, autumn palettes), the tower's light-trace finale takes a different path, ambient details vary (different birds, different lamp colors within districts), the item-04 build grid offers a different valid starting camera framing, and the item-06 invitation copy rotates among curiosity framings. The learner's prior session's builds can appear as faint 'blueprint ghosts' in the tower archive, letting her compare her own past constructions — a self-referential novelty that respects her demonstrated sensitivity to repetition without altering any mathematics. If she previously declined item-06, the reserve-circuit glow on the stadium is the one standing invitation that replays fresh.
visualDirection: Warm-dark engineering aesthetic: deep indigo night valley, amber and gold circuit light, districts in flat-shaded illustrated silhouette with hand-drawn warmth (no corporate flat-design coldness, no toddler pastels — this must read as competent and slightly grown-up for a nine-year-old who asks for harder problems). Countable objects (slices, tulips, stickers, carrots, books, pennants) are high-contrast, evenly spaced, and never decoratively occluded, so counting is always honest — a hard rule given her logic-auditing. Typography: one rounded geometric sans at generous size; equations in a distinct monospaced 'circuit stencil' face so mathematical objects are visually first-class. Layout locked to 1365×768 with no scrolling ever: representation left ~60%, response panel right ~40%, hint toggle bottom-right, valley progress strip along the top edge at ~48px. Tap targets ≥88px. Color is never the sole carrier of correct/incorrect state (current-flow motion plus icon shape carry it) for accessibility.
motionDirection: Motion serves counting and causality, nothing else. Counting pulses are strictly sequential and rhythmic (one object per beat, ~180ms) so skip-counting is physically supported by the animation. Current-flow along wires uses a single bright particle stream, 600–900ms tower-to-district, always completing before feedback text appears so cause precedes explanation. Illumination on success is lamp-by-lamp in product count at an accelerating but still countable cadence. Incorrect flicker is soft and brief (two dim pulses, ~400ms) with zero shake, zero red flash, zero falling/breaking motion. Item-04 placement snaps with a gentle magnetic settle so tap-to-place feels precise without drag skill. No motion ever occurs during the learner's deliberation window except idle ambience (slow tower pulse, drifting clouds) — the world is calm while she thinks. All transitions between districts are a single camera glide ≤1.2s. Every animation is skippable-by-tap after first viewing and respects prefers-reduced-motion by swapping to instant-state changes with the counts still shown discretely.
soundDirection: Sparse, tactile, and honest. Counting ticks: soft wooden marimba tones ascending slightly per count, so a group of 7 sounds like 7 — audio doubles the countability. Commit: a satisfying switch-clack. Correct current: a warm rising hum resolving to a soft chime as lamps light, one faint pluck per lamp at low volume so the product is audible. Incorrect: a neutral low 'hm' tone and the flicker's soft buzz — deliberately unlike any game-over sound, no descending sad motif, honoring the untested-failure-response caveat. Ambient: quiet night crickets shifting toward dawn birdsong as districts light, giving global progress an audible dimension. Item-06's stadium, if entered, earns a distant crowd-murmur warmth on completion. All narration text is also available as spoken audio on tap (positive small-sample evidence for spoken activities), never auto-played mid-deliberation. Full experience functions with sound off; audio is reinforcement, never information's sole carrier.
usefulLibraries: PixiJS (WebGL 2D rendering for the valley scene, current-flow particles, and lamp illumination at 60fps in-iframe)
GSAP (timeline sequencing for counting pulses, current travel, and the finale light-trace)
Howler.js (audio sprites for counting ticks, switch-clack, ambient crossfades, and tap-to-speak narration)
@use-gesture (unified pointer handling so touch and mouse behave identically for tap and tap-to-place)
Zustand (session state: committed answers, preserved builds, district illumination, item-06 election and exit)
canvas-confetti (finale-only celebratory light motes, tuned to the amber palette)
engagementPrediction: High engagement is predicted through item-05 with the strongest signals at item-04, where tap-to-place construction converts the learner from answerer to builder — the moment most aligned with her demonstrated appetite for harder, more autonomous challenge. Specific predictions: (1) she elects item-06 at better-than-even odds when it is framed as the valley's biggest circuit rather than a test, given the harder-riddles evidence; (2) she uses the hint toggle at least once at item-04 or item-06 and continues afterward, matching her riddle-scaffolding pattern; (3) she audits the item-05 factor-order demonstration closely and accepts it because the light-trace makes the referent swap literally countable; (4) session completion through item-07 approaches ceiling because no failure exit exists and the finale is previewed from second one. The main engagement risk window is item-02, the least autonomous item after the orientation's novelty fades; the greenhouse's skip-counting audio rhythm is the designed mitigation.
falsifyingEvidence: This design is falsified by any of the following observed outcomes: (1) the learner declines item-06 AND shows disengagement signals (rushed taps, no hint use, no re-counting) beforehand — falsifying the invitation-framing hypothesis built on riddle evidence; (2) repeated incorrect commits at item-04 followed by abandonment rather than hint requests — falsifying the untested retry-resilience hypothesis (asm-06, 0.5) and confirming the charter's flagged need for an intermediate partially-pre-built rung, which this experience cannot add without a sixth instructional item; (3) the learner treats the flicker-and-return feedback as failure (visible frustration, quitting at first miss) — falsifying the neutral-circuit-tester tone choice; (4) confusion at item-05 where the two-order light-trace is read as 'the same equation twice' rather than a referent swap — falsifying the diegetic demonstration of factor order and confirming asm-04's loose-phrasing trust-cost warning; (5) hint-toggle use at item-01 or item-02 where hints are unnecessary — indicating the 'circuit notes' affordance reads as required content rather than optional tool; (6) construct-vs-read accuracy delta at item-04 substantially exceeding the item-03 baseline — the exact charter concern, which would require upstream packet revision, not creative adjustment.

decisionRecords.decision: Frame the experience as restoring power to a dark valley, with multiplication as the literal electrical law of the world.
decisionRecords.rationale: The academic contract demands mathematics visibly control the world. A circuit metaphor makes groups × amount-per-group causally load-bearing: factors wire the circuit, the product is the countable wattage. It is also age-appropriately competent for a nine-year-old who requests harder challenges, avoiding babyish framing.
alternativesConsidered: Bakery/party themes (rejected: too young-skewing and over-used for equal groups)

Wrestling-tournament theme (rejected: the wrestling evidence is conversational context, not a durable preference conclusion, and competitive framing conflicts with the charter's difficulty-as-failure warning)

decisionRecords.decision: Frame item-06 as a curiosity invitation ('the valley's biggest circuit — yours if you want it') with zero competitive, ranked, or test language, a standing reserve-circuit glow if declined, and a no-cost exit.
decisionRecords.rationale: The charter explicitly flags that the escalation offer's framing is a downstream creative decision and that competitive framing could discourage. asm-02 rests on verbal-puzzle evidence at 0.65 confidence. Curiosity framing preserves the invitation while eliminating the identified discouragement pathway; the standard path still yields a fully restored valley so declining carries no visible penalty.
alternativesConsidered: Hiding item-06 until standard completion (rejected: removes the legible whole-scope promise and makes election feel like an afterthought)

decisionRecords.decision: Incorrect commits produce a neutral flicker-and-return with a diagnostic highlight — no red, no shake, no sad audio, no consoling language.
decisionRecords.rationale: asm-06 is only 0.5 confidence and the retry design is an untested hypothesis; the safest tone is one that carries no failure semantics at all. The circuit 'isn't carrying yet' frames a miss as diagnostic information, which also suits a learner who audits logic and would resent both punishment and condescension.
alternativesConsidered: Encouraging cheerleader feedback (rejected: risks reading as condescending to a challenge-seeking nine-year-old)
Explicit error explanations (rejected: packet incorrectPaths require the learner to re-decide; the system never supplies the decision)

decisionRecords.decision: Demonstrate factor-order equivalence by re-tracing the identical 30 book-lights in two reading orders rather than by verbal explanation.
decisionRecords.rationale: The charter warns that the shelf-groups phrasing carries trust cost if it lands loosely (asm-04), and the learner questions faulty logic. A countable visual demonstration — same 30 lights, two traversal orders, total unchanged — makes the referent swap verifiable by eye without formal property names, staying inside the packet's referentNote exactly.
alternativesConsidered: Text-only referent note (rejected: highest loose-phrasing risk)
Character-narrated analogy (rejected: introduces unverifiable claims a logic-auditing child could contest)

decisionRecords.decision: Present hints as a small 'circuit notes' tool toggle — visually an engineer's instrument, available as an offer in items 02–05 and 07, strictly on-request in item-06, never auto-pushed anywhere.
decisionRecords.rationale: The learner's demonstrated pattern is requesting hints when stuck and continuing after scaffolding; the design must make requesting dignified. Framing hints as an engineer's tool rather than a help lifeline preserves her sense of competence while honoring every item's hintPolicy verbatim, including the rule that no tier states a withheld product.
alternativesConsidered: Auto-surfacing hints after N misses (rejected: violates on-request hintPolicy and the packet's never-push rule in item-06)
No visible hint affordance until first miss (rejected: hides a tool she is known to use proactively)

decisionRecords.decision: Give each item a distinct district, distinct countable objects, distinct micro-mechanics within one constant interaction grammar, and rotate only mutable-layer elements on replay.
decisionRecords.rationale: The learner immediately notices repeated content and it costs trust. All seven packet items are already fresh and non-repeating; the experience layer must match that standard — no reused scenes, no reskinned duplicates — while questions, answers, scope, and difficulty stay frozen per the requirements.
alternativesConsidered: Single reusable classroom scene (rejected: reads as repetition to a repetition-sensitive learner)
Procedurally varied numbers on replay (rejected: forbidden — mathematics is immutable)

decisionRecords.decision: Provide optional tap-to-speak narration for all prompt and feedback text, with counting ticks that make group sizes audible, but keep the full experience functional with sound off.
decisionRecords.rationale: Small-sample feedback was positive for a spoken-pronunciation activity, suggesting spoken audio is welcome but not proven essential; making it optional-by-tap captures the upside with no dependency risk in a possibly muted iframe.
alternativesConsidered: Auto-playing narration (rejected: interrupts deliberation and fails silently when muted)
No audio (rejected: forfeits the skip-counting rhythm support at item-02, the identified engagement risk window)

decisionRecords.decision: Flag rather than resolve both open charter concerns: no intermediate construction rung is added at item-04, and the item-04 accuracy delta plus item-06 election behavior are named as falsifying evidence for upstream review.
decisionRecords.rationale: The requirements forbid changing questions, scope, or difficulty; adding a sixth instructional rung is a packet-level change outside this stage's authority. The correct architect move is to instrument the risk: the design records exactly what observed behavior would confirm the concern and route it upstream.
alternativesConsidered: Smuggling a pre-built partial array into item-04's retry path (rejected: alters scaffold density and violates the immutable-mathematics constraint)
Silently ignoring the concerns (rejected: destroys the audit trail the staged pipeline depends on)

firstThreeSecondsNote: All timings assume asset preload completes before fade-in; a static valley silhouette serves as the loading state so the promise image is present even during load.
